_comment: AutoForm UI for FCS Saturation Calculator using ChiSurf dock areas

sections.label: Scheme
sections.description: Load a photophysical scheme. Presets are starting points, not constraints — every rate, cross-section and brightness stays editable.

sections.label: Laser Power
sections.description:
Total measured laser power Ptotal (mW)
Average excitation power measured at the objective back aperture.
• Photon flux: Φtotal = Ptotal / hν
• Peak focal rate: kexc(0,0) = 2 σabs Φtotal / (π wr²)
At P = 0 the saturated curve is exactly the unsaturated Gaussian.
The slider is logarithmic, because the interesting range spans decades and a linear one would spend all its travel where nothing changes. Drag it to watch the curve respond — results are cached, so revisiting a power is instant.

sections.label: Excitation λ
sections.description:
Excitation wavelength (nm)
Sets the photon energy, so a given power delivers fewer photons at shorter wavelengths, and selects which ε applies. Changing it re-reads ε(λ) when a dye is chosen.

sections.label: Dye (MMFDB)
sections.description:
Read ε from the dye repository
Takes the molar extinction coefficient at the excitation wavelength from the stored absorption spectrum. The catalogued ε is the peak value — exciting off the maximum can deliver a small fraction of it, so this matters. Leave empty to type ε in by hand. Type to search — matching is on any part of the name, so "647" finds every 647 dye.

sections.label: Rate Matrix Units
sections.description: Time base of the transition rates. Changing it rescales the entered values, it does not reinterpret them.

sections.label: Include Bunching Dynamics
sections.description: Include the photokinetic state-relaxation term X(τ), which raises G at lags shorter than the scheme's relaxation times. Switch it off to see the diffusion and volume-expansion effects alone.

sections.label: Number of States
sections.description: Number of states in the photochemical scheme. Two is the minimum (ground + excited); add one state per dark, isomeric or transferred state.

sections.label: Normalize G(τ) to 1.0
sections.description:
Normalize Autocorrelation Curves
Force G(0) = 1.0 to directly highlight and compare shape differences (flatter initial plateau, broader diffusion shift, bunching rise) between unperturbed and saturated curves.

sections.label: 1-component fit
sections.description:
Overlay the fit an experimenter would make
A single 3D-Gaussian diffusion component, fitted to the saturated curve. Saturation flattens the emission profile, and a flat top autocorrelates as a broader mixture of decay rates than any one Gaussian — so this fit comes out too slow and, once the distortion is strong, stops following the curve at all. That deviation is the second apparent diffusion time.

sections.title: Residual against a single diffusion component
sections.description: The saturated curve minus the best single-component 3D-Gaussian fit. A flat line means one diffusion time describes the data; systematic structure is the second, faster component the flattened volume adds.

sections.label: Excitation k(r)
sections.description:
Excitation rate kexc(r), scaled to its peak
The only normalised curve here: a Gaussian exp(-2r²/wr²) shown at 0…1 so its shape can be compared against the populations.

sections.label: State populations
sections.description:
Steady-state populations Pi(r)
One curve per state of the scheme, solved from K(r) P(r) = 0 at every radius. Which state is which is whatever the scheme's labels say — no state is treated specially.

sections.label: Emission Σ Q·P
sections.description:
Emission Σ Qi Pi(r)
The brightness-weighted population — the profile whose spatial autocorrelation is the FCS curve. Plotted on the same absolute scale as the state populations, so with one bright state it lies exactly on that state's curve. Its flattening is the saturation.
